references.text: Isaiah invites all who are thirsty to come to the water – a prophetic parallel to Jesus' offer of living water. [ref:Isa 55:1|Isaiah 55:1]
The Lord refers to himself as the source of living water and accuses his people of having forsaken him. Jesus' offer of living water points back to this image. [ref:Jer 2:13|Jeremiah 2:13]
The Lord is called "the source of living water". Jesus identifies with this source by offering the woman living water. [ref:Jer 17:13|Jeremiah 17:13]
Zechariah's prophecy that living water will flow out from Jerusalem on that day – an eschatological vision to which Jesus' offer of living water connects. [ref:Zech 14:8|Zechariah 14:8]
Jesus explains what the living water is: it becomes a spring within the one who drinks it, welling up with eternal life. [ref:John 4:14|John 4:14]
During the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus declares that whoever is thirsty should come to him and drink, and streams of living water will flow from within the believer. [ref:John 7:37-38|John 7:37-38]
The gift of God that Jesus speaks of has its thematic parallel in God giving (ἔδωκεν) his only Son – the ultimate gift from God. [ref:John 3:16|John 3:16]
Peter uses the same expression "the gift of God" (τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ) toward Simon the sorcerer – the exact linguistic parallel to Jesus' words to the Samaritan woman. [ref:Acts 8:20|Acts 8:20]
Whoever is thirsty may drink from the source of the water of life for free – an eschatological fulfillment of Jesus' offer of living water. [ref:Rev 21:6|Revelation 21:6]
The Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" Whoever is thirsty should come and take the water of life for free – an echo of Jesus' offer to the Samaritan woman. [ref:Rev 22:17|Revelation 22:17]

Paul uses the term "the gift of God's grace" (χάρισμα) regarding eternal life in Christ Jesus – a thematic parallel to Jesus' reference to "the gift of God" (δωρεά), even though a different Greek word is used. [ref:Rom 6:23|Romans 6:23]
Salvation is the gift of God (δῶρον) – grace offered freely, just as Jesus freely offered living water to the Samaritan woman. [ref:Eph 2:8|Ephesians 2:8]
